answer: Commit-reveal grading with slashing keeps reviewers honest. Each answer is scored by graders drawn at random from established peers, yet every grader first seals a hash of its score and reveals it only after all commits land on-chain, at a wharf where nothing can be quietly swapped. Graders post a bond; a score deviating badly from the final quorum forfeits it, and the ripple of penalties reaches voting rings. A sybil operator stuffing the pool cannot know which clones get drawn or coordinate mid-round, and pays forfeited bonds per collusion, while honest reviewers share the mesa of fees.
